failure_policy: Any unsuccessful scheduled main run resets that check's committed consecutive-success sequence before promotion review.

checks.domain: Three named scalar harnesses over the exact domains and assumptions in tests/assurance/manifest.json.
checks.nonclaim: No harness proves ZIP parsing, codecs, filesystem effects, worker containment, cryptography, or behavior outside its stated scalar domain.

checks.domain: Fixed mutations of three pure production scalar kernels under the ordinary sealr library tests.
checks.nonclaim: Mutation outcomes are review leads and never a correctness, completeness, security, or release score.
local_reproduction: cargo-mutants mutants --no-config --package sealr --file crates/sealr/src/interval.rs --file crates/sealr/src/quota.rs --file crates/sealr/src/ratio.rs --re 'CheckedInterval::from_offset_len|QuotaState::consume|ratio_exceeds' --exclude-re 'kani_proofs' --jobs 2 --timeout 120 --output target/assurance-discovery/mutation --no-times --colors never --annotations none --cargo-arg=--locked -- --lib

checks.domain: Source regions observed under the ordinary non-ignored sealr package tests with all features.
checks.nonclaim: Coverage is a discovery map, not evidence of assertion strength, semantic completeness, correctness, or security.

checks.scheduled_job: Bounded worker protocol, semantic-record, and raw portable ustar fuzzing
checks.domain: Digest-pinned protocol, semantic-record, and raw portable ustar seeds plus arbitrary bytes and input-directed checksum-repaired TAR mutations under the workflow's exact bounds.
checks.nonclaim: Coverage-guided fuzzing is heuristic exploration, not exhaustive reachability or proof that the protocol, semantic-record, or TAR interpreters are defect-free.

checks.scheduled_job: 3 GiB sparse gate on each release platform
checks.domain: One exact physically sparse valid 3 GiB ZIP32 fixture on the scheduled Linux, macOS, and Windows runners.
checks.nonclaim: This bounds observed heap use for one fixture and runner generation, not every archive, allocation, filesystem, or platform.
